description: I am a Systems Engineering student from Nicaragua interested in software development, UX/UI, and Earth observation. Through the NASA Space Apps Challenge Universal Event, I aim to explore NASA’s open data and develop an accessible, useful software prototype. I have completed NASA ARSET’s Fundamentals of Remote Sensing course, including practical exercises with NASA Worldview.
summary:
SPHERE is an interactive web-based platform inspired by NASA’s Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. It aims to make astronomical observations more accessible by providing a visual environment where users can explore information related to NASA’s SPHEREx mission and its observations of the universe.

The project combines an accessible user interface with NASA/SPHEREx resources to encourage the exploration and understanding of astronomical data. By presenting complex scientific information through an interactive digital experience, SPHERE seeks to make space science more approachable for students, astronomy enthusiasts, and the general public.

Our goal is to bridge the gap between scientific data and public understanding through technology, web development, and accessible visualization.
details:
Project Overview

SPHERE is an interactive web application developed by NEXUS CARAZO in response to the NASA Space Apps Challenge Planet X and SPHEREx challenge.

The project aims to make astronomical information more accessible through an interactive visual experience inspired by NASA’s SPHEREx mission.

How It Works

SPHERE provides a web-based interface that allows users to interact with the platform and explore astronomical information associated with SPHEREx observations.

The application combines visual elements, interactive components, and NASA-related resources to help users better understand the mission and the scientific information it makes available.

NASA Data and Scientific Resources

The project uses NASA/SPHEREx resources, including information and astronomical data made publicly available through the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA).

These resources provide scientific context and data associated with SPHEREx, a mission designed to survey the entire sky in near-infrared wavelengths across 102 spectral bands.

Technologies and Development

SPHERE was developed as a modern web application using:

  • React 19
  • TypeScript
  • JavaScript
  • HTML5
  • CSS3
  • Vite
  • Node.js and npm
  • Git and GitHub
  • Vercel for deployment

The development process focused on creating an accessible, responsive, and interactive web experience.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of SPHERE is its approach to presenting astronomical information through an accessible digital interface.

Instead of requiring users to navigate complex scientific resources independently, the project aims to provide a more approachable starting point for exploring SPHEREx and its scientific observations.

Intended Impact

SPHERE seeks to encourage public engagement with astronomy, promote interest in NASA scientific missions, and demonstrate how web technologies can help make scientific information more accessible.

The project also provides a foundation for future improvements, including expanded astronomical data exploration and more advanced visualization capabilities.

Future Development

Future improvements could include additional observation comparison tools, expanded data filtering, richer astronomical visualizations, and deeper integration with NASA’s public SPHEREx data services.
